# Story Package: Paul on the Road to Damascus (Acts 9)

**Story Key**: `paulDamascus`

**Position in 365 Roadmap**: Phase 7, Story #29 — Jesus can change even the hardest hearts and use them for good.

---

## Reverent Read-Aloud Retelling (for ages 3–8)

There was a man named Saul who did not love Jesus. In fact, he was very mean to anyone who followed Jesus. He wanted to put them in prison.

One day Saul was traveling on the road to the city of Damascus. He was going there to find more people who loved Jesus and arrest them.

Suddenly, a bright light from heaven flashed around him. He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”

Saul asked, “Who are You, Lord?”

The voice answered, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

When Saul got up, he could not see. His friends had to lead him by the hand into Damascus. For three days he was blind and did not eat or drink.

In Damascus there was a man named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision and told him to go to Saul. Ananias was afraid because he knew Saul was an enemy of Jesus’ followers. But the Lord said, “Go! This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name to the Gentiles and their kings and to the people of Israel.”

Ananias went to Saul, placed his hands on him, and said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

Immediately something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized. From that day on, Saul (who later became known as Paul) became one of the strongest followers of Jesus. He traveled to many places telling people about the love of Jesus.

God can change anyone’s heart — even someone who seems very far away from Him.

---

## Coloring Page Prompt

Simple black-and-white line art for ages 3–8. A man (Saul/Paul) falling to the ground with a bright light shining from heaven. His friends looking surprised and helping him. Later scene of a kind man (Ananias) gently touching his eyes. Soft, miraculous, and hopeful feeling. Clean bold lines with large open spaces.

---

## Read-Along Flow

Color the bright light and the changed man → listen to the story of how Jesus can turn an enemy into a friend and a preacher of the good news → remember that no one is too far away for Jesus to reach and change. Great for praying for people we know who don’t know Jesus yet.

## Quiz — 4 Questions (with helpful scaffolding)

**1. What was Saul doing before he met Jesus on the road?**
- A) Helping people who loved Jesus
- B) Trying to arrest and hurt people who followed Jesus
- C) Building churches
- D) Traveling for fun

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “Saul was actually against Jesus’ followers. He wanted to stop them.”
- If C: “He wasn’t helping the church. He was trying to destroy it.”
- If D: “He was on a mission to find and arrest Christians, not traveling for fun.”

**2. What happened when the bright light flashed around Saul?**
- A) He heard Jesus’ voice speaking to him
- B) He saw nothing special
- C) He ran away and hid
- D) He laughed and kept walking

*Correct: A*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If B: “A very bright light from heaven flashed, and Saul heard Jesus speaking directly to him.”
- If C: “He fell to the ground. Jesus had his full attention.”
- If D: “This was a serious and life-changing moment. Saul was stopped in his tracks.”

**3. What did Ananias do even though he was afraid of Saul?**
- A) He ran away and hid
- B) He went to Saul, placed his hands on him, and helped him receive his sight and the Holy Spirit
- C) He told Saul to go away
- D) He called the soldiers

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “Ananias was scared, but he obeyed Jesus and went to help the man who had been his enemy.”
- If C: “He went with kindness and called Saul ‘brother.’ Jesus had changed everything.”
- If D: “He trusted Jesus’ instructions and became the one who helped Saul see again — both physically and spiritually.”

**4. What does Saul’s story help us remember?**
- A) That some people are too mean for Jesus to love
- B) That Jesus can change even the hardest hearts and use them to tell many people about His love
- C) That we should stay away from people who don’t know Jesus
- D) That bright lights are always scary

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “Saul became Paul and told thousands of people about Jesus. No heart is too hard for Jesus to change.”
- If C: “Paul’s story shows us that God can use anyone — even former enemies — to share the good news.”
- If D: “The light was part of God getting Saul’s attention so he could be changed forever.”
